## data prep

the dataset is loaded and curred. We remove adult = 0 and NAs

```{r}
data250_apisum_00 <- read.csv("../../../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/01.acyrthosiphon_pisum_P123amp_on_faba_collection/acyrthospipon_pisum_fecundity_on_faba_collection.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep = ",") %>%  
  mutate(ivip = as.factor(ivip)) %>% 
  mutate(session = as.factor(session)) 



data250_apisum_01 <- data250_apisum_00 %>% filter(!is.na(larvae_total_number))
data250_apisum_01$ivip <- droplevels(data250_apisum_01$ivip)

data250_apisum_02<- data250_apisum_01 %>% filter(adult_alive != "0") #remove if no adult
data250_apisum_02$ivip <- droplevels(data250_apisum_02$ivip)

data250_apisum_02$ivip <-as.factor(data250_apisum_02$ivip)


```
Once we have removed the NAs and all rows for which we don't have an adult, we can still make adjustments to the dataset. We can remove outliers to ensure that our distribution approaches a normal distribution, and we can also filter out genotypes based on a threshold for the minimum number of repetitions required to keep a genotype.
We have 3 methods to handle outliers: 1)keep the outliers; 2)remove manually the outliers based on biological reasons; 3) use the interquartile range method (IQR) to remove all data outside a specific range.

The goal of this script is to study how our model reacts to changes in the outlier removal method and the minimum number of repetitions required to retain a genotype.

in the folowing loop we varry two parameters, i the minimal number of reps for the genotypes and the outlier filtering method.

function to calculate all metric used to compare filters
```{r}
analyze_filtered_data <- function(data, i, filter_name) {
  data <- data %>%
    group_by(ivip) %>%
    filter(n() >= i) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    droplevels()

  if (nrow(data) < 5 || nlevels(data$ivip) < 2) {
    return(NULL)  # skip iterations with too little data
  }

  NGEN <- nlevels(data$ivip)
  n_after <- nrow(data)

  # Fit the model
  mod <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ ivip + (1|session/block), data = data)
  residuals_values <- residuals(mod)
  RMSE <- sqrt(mean(residuals_values^2))
  shapiro_res <- shapiro.test(residuals_values)$p.value
  shapiro <- shapiro.test(data$larvae_total_number)$p.value

  # Heritability model
  mod_h2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | ivip) + (1 | session), data = data)
  estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
  genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
  residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]
  nbE <- nlevels(data$session)
  H2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))

  return(data.frame(
    filter = filter_name, i = i, RMSE = RMSE, n_after = n_after,
    H2 = H2, shapiro = shapiro, shapiro_res = shapiro_res, NGEN = NGEN
  ))
}
```

## analyse of the filtered datasets
```{r}

# Initialize an empty data frame to store results
results <- data.frame(x = numeric(0), i = numeric(0), RMSE = numeric(0), 
                       n_after = numeric(0), H2=numeric(0),shapiro=numeric(0),shapiro_res=numeric(0),NGEN=numeric(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


###filter based on IQR
    # Calculate IQR and bounds for outlier removal
    IQR_value <- IQR(data250_apisum_02$larvae_total_number)
    lower_bound <- quantile(data250_apisum_02$larvae_total_number, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR_value
    upper_bound <- quantile(data250_apisum_02$larvae_total_number, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR_value
    filter ="IQR"
    # Filter out outliers
    data_iqr <- data250_apisum_02[data250_apisum_02$larvae_total_number >= lower_bound & data250_apisum_02$larvae_total_number <= upper_bound, ]
    

for (i in 2:9) {
  res <- analyze_filtered_data(data_iqr, i, filter_name = "IQR")
  if (!is.null(res)) results <- rbind(results, res)
}

for (i in 2:9) {
  res <- analyze_filtered_data(data250_apisum_02, i, filter_name = "no_filter")
  if (!is.null(res)) results <- rbind(results, res)
    }
    
data_manual<- data250_apisum_02 %>% filter(larvae_total_number != "0") 

for (i in 2:9) {
  res <- analyze_filtered_data(data_manual, i, filter_name = "Manual_filter")
  if (!is.null(res)) results <- rbind(results, res)
}

print(results)
```
Based on these results it seems appropriate to select the IQR filter as it yield best heritability, lower RMSE and more normal data.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
write.csv(x = results, 
          file = "filter_annalysis.csv", 
          quote = F, row.names = F)

```

```{r}
iqr_results <- results %>% filter(filter == "IQR")
```

We now need to visualize the data we generated from the IQR filter to choose the best value for i (minimal number of repetitions to keep a genotype)

## Advanced visualisation of the data generated
```{r}

ggplot(iqr_results, aes(x = i, y = NGEN)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,13,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,250)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = NGEN), arrow = T) +
  labs(x = "N biological replicates", y = "N genotypes") +
  ggtitle("N genotypes = f(N biological replicates)")

y<-as.vector(iqr_results$NGEN)
x<-as.vector(iqr_results$i)

# Compute slope (finite differences)
slope <- diff(y) / diff(x)

# To align slopes with x-values, use midpoints
x_mid <- (x[-1] + x[-length(x)]) / 2

# Plot slope (derivative)
plot(x_mid, slope, type = "b", col = "red", main = "Numerical Derivative (Slope)",
     ylab = "Slope", xlab = "x")
abline(h = 0, col = "gray", lty = 2)  # reference line for zero slope



```


Based on the variation in genotype number the best i value seems to be 6
